steps.say: We call cart_total([3, 4]) and want to keep the answer in bill.
The loop adds 3, then 4, so total is 7.
print puts 7 on the screen, but the function hands nothing back.
steps.error_label: Bug: print is not return. The caller receives None.

steps.say: The call ends. bill gets None, because there was no return.
None + 1 raises TypeError. With return total on line 5, bill would be 7.

pages.title: print shows, return gives back
paragraphs: print writes a value on the screen for a person to read. return hands a value back to the line that called the function.
A function with no return gives back None. If the caller stores the result, it stores None, and the next line that uses it breaks.

key_term.definition: the value a function hands back to the line that called it.

pages.title: return ends the function
paragraphs: The moment Python reaches a return, the function stops, even in the middle of a loop.
A return False inside a loop gives up after the first item. Put it after the loop, once every item has been checked.

inner.label: if letter in 'aeiou':
lines: return True   (ends the function at once)

key_term.definition: leaving a function before its last line because the answer is already known.

transcript: print and return look similar, but they do different jobs.
print shows a value on the screen for you to read.
return hands the value back to whoever called the function.
If a function never returns, the caller gets None.
return also ends the function straight away, even inside a loop.
So put return False after the loop, once every item has been checked.
